# Lucy Darling
## Overview
*     
*
Award-winning performer Carisa Hendrix captivates audiences around the world as charming socialite and cocktail enthusiast Lucy Darling, bringing her razor-sharp wit, vivacious energy and skillful magic to the stage. Currently touring with her show Simply Darling, Hendrix continues Lucy’s mischievous adventures with a captivating variety show filled with sophisticated humor and plenty of delightful surprises.
Joining Lucy is TJ Shanoff, a hilarious musical improviser from Chicago’s legendary home of improv comedy, The Second City. With his playful piano melodies and perfectly timed musical wit, TJ adds an extra layer of humor to Lucy’s sophisticated sarcasm, rewarding careful listeners with an inside joke or two. Blending magic, comedy, and music, Simply Darling brings Lucy’s signature charm and mischief from screen to stage. It’s a chance to step away from reality, embrace the unexpected and indulge in the wonder, laughter, and mischief we all deserve.
_**Notice:** Latecomers will be seated at the discretion of management. Entry and seating may be delayed until an appropriate break in the performance, and original seat locations cannot be guaranteed._
_By purchasing tickets and/or attending the show, you consent to being photographed, filmed, and/or otherwise recorded. Your attendance constitutes your consent to such photography, filming, and recording, and to the unrestricted use of your likeness, voice, and name in any and all media, worldwide, in perpetuity, for any purpose in connection with the production._

Charlie and The Darlings is a genre-spanning band consisting of some of NYC’s most talented musicians and comedians. Dance the night away to the joyful and silly beats reminiscent of The Electric Mayhem (yes, the band from the Muppets), The Village People, Prince, and The B52’s.

##### FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 13
DOORS @ 6:30PM | SHOW @ 7PM
ARS NOVA
511 W 54TH STREET

Charlie O'Connor
Charlie O’Connor is a British musician and performer based in NYC. When he’s not composing music for other people (Emily Wilson, Chloe Troast, PDD, Zach and Drew) he is working on his own goofy musical projects.
Where does the show take place?
This show will take place at Ars Nova, located at 511 W 54th Street, New York, NY 10019.
What is the seating set-up & how do I get the best seats?
Seating is general admission and first-come first-served. So, the earlier you arrive at the theater, the more choice you’ll have about where you sit! (Bonus: cheapest drinks in Midtown are at Bars Nova!)
The only way to guarantee you reserved seats is to become a Super Nova. Super Novas never hear “sold out,” get reserved seats in prime locations, and make fair wages and accessible tickets possible. Learn more about becoming a Super Nova here!
How much are tix?
Tix to this show are Name Your Price starting at $15, meaning you decide what you pay! We take a small portion of ticket sales to pay for the show’s front-of-house and theater technicians then pass on the rest of the single ticket revenue directly to the show’s lead artists. You can learn more about What’s Ars Is Yours: Name Your Price Tix by visiting ourHow We Do It page.
What if it's sold out?

#### Charlie O'Connor
##### FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 13
If a performance is sold out, you can join a standby line for day-of-show tix made available by minute cancellations and no-shows. Standby will begin 1 hour prior to curtain and will form outsideFolks from the standby line will be admitted into the show on a rolling basis as availability is confirmed. Standby tix are name-your-price starting at $5 + fees.
How does Name Your Price tix work?
Once you’ve selected your performance date and time at check-out, you’ll see a number of ticket price options ranging from $15 to $100. Select the price point you want to pay and the number of tickets you’d like to purchase and they’ll be added to your cart. After that, continue through the check-out process and you’ll be all set!
Are there ticket fees?
Yes. The processing fees are charged by our ticketing and credit card processors, and increase along with the base price of your ticket.
What is your refund/exchange policy?
All sales are final – there are no refunds or exchanges.
If you’re unable to use your tickets, you may donate them in exchange for a letter of tax credit by emailing tix@arsnovanyc.com.
What if I feel sick?
We ask that you **stay home if you aren’t feeling well** or are awaiting the results of a COVID test. Please let us know prior to your ticketed performance, and we will work with you to find a solution if you’re unable to attend.
What are your COVID safety protocols?
We welcome and encourage mask-wearing to protect yourself and others. However, as mask mandates have lifted and city, state and federal guidelines have changed, **we will not be requiring them at performances.**
**We no longer require proof of vaccination**, but we strongly encourage all audience members to get vaccinated and boosted in accordance with public health guidelines.
Our staff will clean and sanitize the theater and common areas and we’ll continue to provide hand sanitizer for your personal use.
Signage is posted in all spaces encouraging washing or sanitizing hands frequently.
A note on content advisories:

#### Charlie O'Connor
##### FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 13
Ars Nova is uncensored. We provide content advisories — to the best of our ability — to inform audiences when shows contain racial violence, racist language, sexual violence or nudity. We provide information about this type of content in advance, based on our core values, so that each audience member can make an informed decision about if and how they’d like to engage with that content. We welcome artists to share additional information about their shows based on their own core values.
Mobility Needs
Ars Nova is wheelchair accessible. If you wish or need to remain in your wheelchair throughout the show, our staff will remove the theater chair. This can be done by letting us know your needs/plans in advance; just email[Declan Zhang](mailto:%20tix@arsnovanyc.com). It can also be done without prior notice when you arrive! If you wish to transfer to the theater seat from your wheelchair, we are happy to store your wheelchair or motorized mobility aid in the lobby during the performance. The House Manager will return your mobility device to you at the end of the performance as this show has no intermission.
About 25% of the seating is on the ground floor of the theater and does not require using stairs to access. There are five six-inch steps to get into the building.
All remaining seats require no less than one and no more than three steps to access.
Service Animals
Licensed service animals (any dogs that are trained to do work or perform tasks for people with disabilities) are welcome at Ars Nova. They must rest in your seating area throughout the performance and are unable to occupy the aisle. Please bring proof of certification or a license for your service animal and be prepared to present it to the House Manager upon request. You can send advance notice to [Declan Zhang](mailto: tix@arsnovanyc.com), which is appreciated, but not required.
Restrooms
Our bathrooms are stalled, all gender restrooms – everyone is welcome to use any bathroom of their choice. We have two single-person restrooms in the lobby; with the wheelchair accessible option located right outside the theater on the first floor (doors 7 feet 10 inches x 3 feet 10.5 inches).
Resources for Parents

#### Charlie O'Connor
##### FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 13
We have space that can be made to offer privacy for feeding should you need at any time. See the House Manager onsite and they will arrange a comfortable space, with storage and refrigeration for your materials.
Seat Style, Spacing & Dimensions
The audience seating locations could be in, around and throughout the playing area. Performers will be within 3’ of you.
The seating is a combination of chairs.
Black Chairs with back: 19” wide x 32.25” high x 21.75” deep with a 500lb capacity
Black Counter height: 16.5” wide x 38” high x 18” deep with a 500lb capacity
The doors for entry into the building are 7 feet 10.5 inches x 3 feet 7 inches (external) and 7 feet 10 inches x feet 10.5 inches (internal).
Box Office height is 3 feet 6 inches and the Bar height is 3 feet 8.5 inches.

**David Darling** (March 4, 1941 – January 8, 2021)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Darling_(musician)#cite_note-Phares-1) was an American cellist and composer. In 2010, he won the Grammy Award for Best New Age Album. He performed and recorded with Bobby McFerrin, Paul Winter Consort, Ralph Towner and Spyro Gyra and released many solo albums. Among these were 15 recordings for ECM.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Darling_(musician)#cite_note-2)
Darling was born on March 4, 1941, in Elkhart, Indiana. He was interested in music from an early age, beginning piano when he was four, cello at ten, and string bass in high school. He studied classical cello at Indiana State University and after graduating remained there another four years as a teacher.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Darling_(musician)#cite_note-Phares-1)

He worked as a studio musician in Nashville, Tennessee and was a member of the Paul Winter Consort until 1978. During the following year, he was part of the chamber jazz group Gallery with Ralph Towner and released his first solo album, Journal October.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Darling_(musician)#cite_note-Phares-1)
Darling's performance and composition draw on a wide range of styles, including classical, jazz, Brazilian, African, and Indian music.
He wrote and performed music for more than a dozen major motion pictures, the horror film _[Child's Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child's\_Play\_(1988\_film) "Child's Play (1988 film)")_ (1988), _Heat_ (1995), and _Until the End of the World_ (1991). He contributed music to _Nouvelle Vague_ (1990), _[Éloge de l'amour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89loge\_de\_l'amour "Éloge de l'amour")_ (2001), and _Notre musique_ (2004).
In 2000, he recorded a collaboration with the Wulu Bunun, a group of Taiwanese aborigines.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Darling_(musician)#cite_note-3)
In 2007 he recorded _The Darling Conversations_, with Julie Weber discussing his music philosophy. It was issued by Manifest Spirit Records. In January 2009, Darling released the Grammy-winning _Prayer for Compassion_, a follow-up of his earlier _8-String Religion_, both on the Curve Blue label.
In 1986, Darling joined Young Audiences, an organization that seeks to educate children about music and the arts through school programs. In the same year, he founded Music for People, which seeks to encourage self-expression through musical improvisation. His teaching methods are the subject of a book, _Return to Child_ (2008).

In May 2008, he became part of a collaboration of music teacher and performers offering a training program in holistic and intercultural approaches to healing with sound and music at the New York Open Center Sound and Music School. David Darling died in his sleep, January 8, 2021.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Darling_(musician)#cite_note-4)

Title: About Me — Rara Darling
Chunks: 0
Rara Darling is a New York City based Burlesque Performer, Event Producer, & creator of mind-blowing cabaret style spectacles! Known as the "Snack that Smiles Back," Rara Darling's burlesque style ranges from energetic campy to sultry classic to outrageous and raunchy neo-burlesque. No matter the style, Rara sees each performance as an opportunity to tell a story through subversive movement and striptease.
Rara is the Founder, Director and Creative Producer of Events by Darling. For the last 7 years Rara has and continues to produce countless shows, events & parties of all kinds that are open to the public to enjoy! They are also regularly hired to produce shows and entertainment for private events. Rara believes in the power of facilitated connection through mind-expanding experiences and works tirelessly towards this goal.
Rara is the Director of Special Events and resident producer and performer at the world-renowned House of Yes.Through thier position at House of Yes Rara has produced epic cabarets, weddings, birthdays, b’mitzvahs, fundraisers, brand launches, corporate events and more! They have worked with companies such as Bacardi, Duolingo, Kiehl’s among others.
Known as a professional spectacle maker, Rara Darling can make any event, big or small, one that you will never forget.

**Carisa Hendrix** (born 1987) is a Canadian magician, comedian, and fire eater who often performs in the persona of **Lucy Darling**, inspired by the wisecracking socialite characters from the Golden Age of Hollywood.
Hendrix was born in Prince Albert, Saskatchewan, in 1987.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-allabout-2) They[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-4) grew up and are based in Calgary.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-allabout-2)
Hendrix's interest in magic began while watching a David Copperfield special with their father at the age of six or seven.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-Davis-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:1-6) Later, while volunteering at a library, they created a well-received magic trick involving library cards.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-Davis-5)

At the age of 16, Hendrix was kicked out of the family home. Needing to make money, they worked a variety of retail jobs, and at a haunted house for $50 per night, performing a ten minute set using skills learned from sideshow performers at a youth summer arts program, such as fire eating.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-Davis-5)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:0-1)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:2-7)
Hendrix began booking gigs, learning additional skills such as stilt walking, which allowed them to leave retail jobs and focus on performing. They incorporated a comedic flair, combining magic with circus arts.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:2-7)
In 2007, Hendrix was accepted at the Alberta College of Art and Design, studying a variety of performance skills including acting, magic, vaudeville, burlesque and modeling.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:3-8)
Their career skyrocketed following an invitation by an Italian world record television show to break the record for Torch Teething, which is holding a flaming torch between the teeth.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:2-7)
Hendrix identifies as gay, non-binary, and a drag queen.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-9)
Hendrix was the subject of the 2016 Super Channel documentary _Girl on Fire._[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:3-8)

Hendrix has been profiled in major media for their success in magic, a field which has historically been male dominated.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-whosthat-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-13)
Hendrix has been featured repeatedly at the Melbourne Magic Festival.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-14)
In 2019, Hendrix was named artist-in-residence at the Chicago Magic Lounge and appeared on the _Penn and Teller: Fool Us_ television show.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-17)
In 2020, Hendrix was featured in the Calgary Herald "Celebrating 20 inspiring and compelling Calgarians."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:0-1)
As of October 2025, Hendrix has 1.5 million TikTok followers.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:4-18)
Hendrix during a pre-show talkback
In December 2025, Hendrix performed at the MGM Grand Las Vegas Underground Theatre with Sarah Hester Ross.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:4-18)

Hendrix is a regular performer at The Magic Castle, in Hollywood, California, performing as Lucy Darling, the Mistress of Magic: a sharp-tongued, comedic magician partly based on Dorothy Parker.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:1-6)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-whosthat-11)

## Awards and recognition
[edit]
In 2012, Hendrix set the Guinness World Record[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-19) for torch teething,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-20) which was featured in both the _Guinness Book of World Records_ in 2014, and _[Ripley's Believe it or Not!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ripley's\_Believe\_it\_or\_Not! "Ripley's Believe it or Not!")_ in 2015.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-21)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:2-7) The fire was held in their mouth for two minutes and one second.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-:2-7)
In 2017, Hendrix won the Melbourne International Comedy Festival Award[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-22) and the Award for Best Comedy Show at The Melbourne Magic Festival.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-23) In 2019, they won the Slaight Family Foundation's Canadian Rising Star Award.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carisa_Hendrix#cite_note-25)

## Who is Carisa Hendrix?
#### The Award-Winning, World Record-Breaking
person behind the international sensation, Lucy Darling.
Carisa Hendrix is a respected variety artist who brings magic, mischief, and mayhem to the stage with their highly reviewed semi-improvised performances.
This larger-than-life performer has earned accolades for their delightful comedic flair and amazing magical stunts. Well-loved in the world of variety arts, Hendrix has won countless different awards and thrilled audiences worldwide.
Lucy Darling is Hendrix's most recognizable creation. Born at the Melbourne Magic Festival in 2017, Lucy is a charming vintage Hollywood socialite known for her impeccable wit, playful mischief, and exceptionally good hair.
As Lucy Darling, Hendrix has toured the world, delighting audiences of all sizes --- but in December of 2024, everything changed when a clip from a recent show went viral on TikTok, amassing millions of views.
Soon, Lucy became an internet sensation across several social media platforms: the Lucy Family Tree is now made up of more than 4 million followers. In 2025 alone, more than 50,000 people attended live Lucy Darling performances, many of which were completely sold out.
Even before Lucy emerged on the scene, Hendrix was already well established in the world of magic, circus, and variety arts. At 16, Hendrix's interest in the carnival sideshow was sparked by a chance encounter with an elderly performer and the misguided support of a high school chum. After only a few months of training, they began doing small shows, and despite the unpolished quality, the bookings kept coming in.
After high school, Hendrix worked as a children's educator & program director at not-for-profit organizations, but it was too late; their love for performing was apparent. As rewarding as teaching was, the shiny allure of the stage was just too enticing.

Hendrix has always been an avid learner and studied acting, dance, comedy, circus, prop manipulation, vaudeville, burlesque, modeling, and magic. LA rockers The Darlings have come a long way since their inception in 2005. After beating out hundreds of bands to win this year’s Ernie Ball Battle of the Bands, the Darlings had their song “What Lies Below” picked up by the Anaheim Ducks, who used the track for their 09/10 season promo spots on Prime Ticket. The band’s song “Let’s Roll” has also been in steady rotation on influential LA modern rock station KROQ’s Locals Only show for months. In addition to taking part in the Vans Warped Tour for the third time last summer and securing endorsements from Ernie Ball and Hart & Huntington, they hit the road on tours with Pennywise and Guttermouth. The Darlings latest release, The New Escape melds the individual members’ classic rock and alternative influences into a hearty dose of honest and pure, rock and roll that steers clear of trends and posturing. Stand out songs include "Let's Roll" "Hypnotize" "Untitled" and "Broken Heart Still Beating."

Greyhound Canada is relocating its passenger stations in Regina and Saskatoon as the province moves to sell the former Saskatchewan Transportation Company stations.

## Company has to move because current locations are in soon-to-be-sold Sask. Transportation Company depots
Stephanie Taylor · CBC News
· Posted: Sep 09, 2017 7:00 AM EDT | Last Updated: September 9, 2017
Listen to this article
Estimated 2 minutes
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.
The province is selling off former Saskatchewan Transportation Company depots in Regina and Saskatoon, which means Greyhound Canada is moving its passenger service stops.(Jason Warick/CBC)
Starting this fall, passengers using Greyhound Canada in Regina and Saskatoon will be catching their buses at different stops.
The province is selling off former bus depots, land and other proprieties that belonged to the Saskatchewan Transportation Company.
Greyhound Canada has continued operating passenger services out of the defunct STC stations in Saskatoon and Regina but the province's contract with the company comes to an end on Sept. 29.
*   **Former STC bus depots up for sale in Saskatoon, Moose Jaw, Regina, Prince Albert**  
*   **What could become of STC depots?**
In Saskatoon, Greyhound is moving its passenger service to the Husky Travel Center at 315 Marquis Dr., where it will start offering service on Sept.30, according to a company spokesperson.
Greyhound Canada will be offering the following trips to and from its new location in Saskatoon:
*   Two westbound trips to Edmonton — departures at 8:15 a.m and 4:30 p.m.  
*   One eastbound trip from Edmonton — departure at 1:30 p.m.  
*   One eastbound trip to Winnipeg — departs at 8:10 a.m.
Spokesperson Lanesha Gipson wrote in an email to CBC that passenger service will continue operating in Regina, but details about where the new stop will be are still being finalized.

## Still no direct service between Regina, Saskatoon
She said service on the Trans-Canada and Yellowhead highways would remain the same after the company's contract with the province expires, and prospective passengers should checkthe company's website for routes and times.
Passenger and freight service will continue in Swift Current, Yorkton and Moose Jaw, Sask., Gipson wrote.
She said there will still be no direct service offered between Regina and Saskatoon as passengers will be able to travel to these cities on Greyhound routes to Edmonton and Winnipeg.

The province is selling off former Saskatchewan Transportation Company depots in Regina and Saskatoon, which means Greyhound Canada is moving its passenger service stops.(Jason Warick/CBC)
Starting this fall, passengers using Greyhound Canada in Regina and Saskatoon will be catching their buses at different stops.
The province is selling off former bus depots, land and other proprieties that belonged to the Saskatchewan Transportation Company.
Greyhound Canada has continued operating passenger services out of the defunct STC stations in Saskatoon and Regina but the province's contract with the company comes to an end on Sept. 29.
*   **Former STC bus depots up for sale in Saskatoon, Moose Jaw, Regina, Prince Albert**  
*   **What could become of STC depots?**
In Saskatoon, Greyhound is moving its passenger service to the Husky Travel Center at 315 Marquis Dr., where it will start offering service on Sept.30, according to a company spokesperson.
Greyhound Canada will be offering the following trips to and from its new location in Saskatoon:
*   Two westbound trips to Edmonton — departures at 8:15 a.m and 4:30 p.m.  
*   One eastbound trip from Edmonton — departure at 1:30 p.m.  
*   One eastbound trip to Winnipeg — departs at 8:10 a.m.
Spokesperson Lanesha Gipson wrote in an email to CBC that passenger service will continue operating in Regina, but details about where the new stop will be are still being finalized.

Passenger and freight service will continue in Swift Current, Yorkton and Moose Jaw, Sask., Gipson wrote.
She said there will still be no direct service offered between Regina and Saskatoon as passengers will be able to travel to these cities on Greyhound routes to Edmonton and Winnipeg.

Greyhound Canada is relocating its passenger stations in Regina and Saskatoon as the province moves to sell the former Saskatchewan Transportation Company stations.

## Company has to move because current locations are in soon-to-be-sold Sask. Transportation Company depots
Stephanie Taylor · CBC News
· Posted: Sep 09, 2017 7:00 AM EDT | Last Updated: September 9, 2017
Listen to this article
Estimated 2 minutes
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.
The province is selling off former Saskatchewan Transportation Company depots in Regina and Saskatoon, which means Greyhound Canada is moving its passenger service stops.(Jason Warick/CBC)
Starting this fall, passengers using Greyhound Canada in Regina and Saskatoon will be catching their buses at different stops.
The province is selling off former bus depots, land and other proprieties that belonged to the Saskatchewan Transportation Company.
Greyhound Canada has continued operating passenger services out of the defunct STC stations in Saskatoon and Regina but the province's contract with the company comes to an end on Sept. 29.
*   **Former STC bus depots up for sale in Saskatoon, Moose Jaw, Regina, Prince Albert**  
*   **What could become of STC depots?**
In Saskatoon, Greyhound is moving its passenger service to the Husky Travel Center at 315 Marquis Dr., where it will start offering service on Sept.30, according to a company spokesperson.
Greyhound Canada will be offering the following trips to and from its new location in Saskatoon:
*   Two westbound trips to Edmonton — departures at 8:15 a.m and 4:30 p.m.  
*   One eastbound trip from Edmonton — departure at 1:30 p.m.  
*   One eastbound trip to Winnipeg — departs at 8:10 a.m.
Spokesperson Lanesha Gipson wrote in an email to CBC that passenger service will continue operating in Regina, but details about where the new stop will be are still being finalized.

## Still no direct service between Regina, Saskatoon
She said service on the Trans-Canada and Yellowhead highways would remain the same after the company's contract with the province expires, and prospective passengers should checkthe company's website for routes and times.
Passenger and freight service will continue in Swift Current, Yorkton and Moose Jaw, Sask., Gipson wrote.
She said there will still be no direct service offered between Regina and Saskatoon as passengers will be able to travel to these cities on Greyhound routes to Edmonton and Winnipeg.
